findings.claim: summonReviewer reuses the worker's summon (loopSummon with the starter's paddock/lane), so each reviewer starts inside the loop worktree, which settle has just reset to `judged`; a fresh agent there loads the CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/settings.json and hooks that the working agent committed, so the agent shapes who judges it and can even run hooks in the reviewer's session. That breaks the PRD's central anti-goal, even though the persona and spec text do come from `before`.
findings.fix: Start reviewers outside the worktree, in a folder with no agent-controlled config (a temporary checkout of `before`, or an empty folder under the daemon), with a read-only sandbox, and add a test where the agent commits a CLAUDE.md and the reviewer does not see it.

findings.claim: Reviewers are left out of loopOthersWorking because they 'only read text', but nothing enforces that: they run in the worktree with the worker's write sandbox, and after reviewDone the machine goes straight to decide/markDone without measuring the tree again. A reviewer that edits or commits after settle leaves an adopted HEAD or a dirty tree that no check or gate ever ran on, and the othersWorking guard cannot catch it.
findings.fix: After the dismiss in WorkLoopReview (line 105), confirm `rev-parse HEAD == judged` and a clean `status --porcelain`, and fail the attempt with 'o revisor mexeu na árvore' if not; or make the reviewer's sandbox read-only.

findings.claim: When the daemon stops in the middle of a review, the cancelled asks turn every persona mute, and `.runReview` writes `reviewRejects += 1` and a note 'revisor X sem resposta' before it returns. `judges()` (line 354) also lacks `.reviewDone`, so this fake refusal reaches the machine as a verdict. It survives the later uncount, and in the next run the task's first real refusal defers it as 'recusada duas vezes'.
findings.fix: Add `.reviewDone` to `judges()`, and inside `.runReview` return `.cancelled` with no record when `Task.isCancelled`, before writing reviewRejects or the note.

findings.claim: `reviewRejects` is stored on the task and goes back to 0 only on an approval. Task reopen and a new `work run` never clear it, so a task the owner reopens after 'chame o dono' is deferred again on its first refusal, and a check failure between two refusals still counts them as 'seguidas'.
findings.fix: Set reviewRejects to 0 when the task is reopened, when it is deferred by twiceRefused, and on any attempt that fails before the review; add one test for reopen followed by a single refusal.

findings.claim: The reviewer's turn is `min(timeout, left)`, and `left` is at least 1 s, so when the budget is spent every persona gets ~1 s, comes back mute, and the budget running out is counted as a review refusal (reviewRejects+1, which feeds twiceRefused).
findings.fix: When `left` is under a minimum, end the attempt for lack of budget instead of 'revisor sem resposta', and do not count it in reviewRejects.

findings.claim: A reviewer goes into loopReviewers only after `summon` returns (loopReviewerBorn). Until then its terminal is already in ws.terminals unmarked, and another loop in the same paddock that calls loopOthersWorking during the agent's boot can count it as working.
findings.fix: Reserve the name and id as a reviewer before the terminal is created (pass a reviewer flag to loopSummon), or mark it inside loopSummon.

findings.claim: A daemon that falls mid-review leaves the reviewer terminals alive, and loopReviewers lives only in memory, so after a restart they count as 'outro agente trabalhando' and stop the loop that comes back (the ponytail comment names the leak but leaves the effect on othersWorking unhandled).
findings.fix: Name reviewers with a recognizable suffix or record them in the Work, and dismiss them in the loop's start sweep.
